session_game.title: Job Interview Simulator
session_game.description: Face realistic AI interviewers. Practice answering tough questions, handling pressure, and landing your dream job.

help_content.what_is: A job interview simulator where you face AI interviewers with different styles — from friendly HR to tough technical leads. Practice answering behavioral questions, explaining your strengths, and handling curveball questions.
tips: Use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result
Research the company before the interview
Prepare your 'Tell me about yourself' answer
Ask thoughtful questions at the end
Be specific — use numbers and examples

communication_clarity.description: Were answers clear, concise, and well-structured?

relevant_experience.description: Did they effectively connect their experience to the role?

confidence_composure.description: Did they stay composed under pressure?

problem_solving.description: How did they approach hypothetical problems?

cultural_fit.description: Did they demonstrate alignment with company values?

enthusiasm_interest.description: Did they show genuine interest in the role?

persona_pool.name: Meera Kapoor
persona_pool.focus: cultural fit, motivation, teamwork, career goals
persona_pool.personality: Warm and encouraging. Puts candidates at ease but notices inconsistencies. Values authenticity over rehearsed answers.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Tell me about a time you failed at something. What did you learn?

persona_pool.name: Arjun Reddy
persona_pool.focus: problem-solving, technical depth, analytical thinking, learning ability
persona_pool.personality: Direct and analytical. Asks follow-up questions to test depth of knowledge. Respects candidates who admit what they don't know.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Walk me through how you'd design a solution for this problem from scratch.

persona_pool.name: Deepak Malhotra
persona_pool.personality: Experienced and observant. Looks for leadership potential even in junior candidates. Tests decision-making with scenario questions.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: You have two team members in conflict. Walk me through exactly how you handle it.

persona_pool.name: Nisha Agarwal
persona_pool.personality: Fast-paced and energetic. Values people who take initiative. Hates 'that's not my job' mentality. Looks for scrappy problem-solvers.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Our product launch is in 2 weeks and the lead developer just quit. What do you do?

persona_pool.name: Dr. Shalini Prasad
persona_pool.focus: self-awareness, emotional intelligence, growth mindset, resilience
persona_pool.personality: Calm and probing. Uses silence effectively. Asks 'why' multiple times to get to real motivations. Values self-awareness above all.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: What's your biggest weakness, and I want the real one, not a disguised strength.

persona_pool.name: Vikram Singh
persona_pool.focus: pressure handling, quick thinking, composure, conviction
persona_pool.personality: Deliberately challenging. Interrupts, challenges answers, plays devil's advocate. Tests if candidates crack under pressure or stay composed.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: I'm not convinced. Why should we hire you over the 200 other applicants?

persona_pool.name: Riya Sharma
persona_pool.focus: values alignment, diversity awareness, team dynamics, work-life balance
persona_pool.personality: Passionate about workplace culture. Tests whether candidates genuinely care about values or just say the right things. Notices subtle cues.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Describe a time you stood up for something you believed in, even when it was unpopular.

persona_pool.name: Amit Joshi
persona_pool.personality: Polished and articulate. Evaluates how candidates would represent the company. Tests communication skills with role-play scenarios.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: An angry client calls threatening to leave. Role-play how you handle this call right now.

persona_pool.name: Priya Menon
persona_pool.focus: attention to detail, process orientation, quality, consistency
persona_pool.personality: Meticulous and thorough. Catches vague answers immediately. Values candidates who give specific examples with dates, numbers, and outcomes.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: You said you improved sales by 'a lot.' Give me the exact percentage and the time period.

persona_pool.name: Karan Mehta
persona_pool.focus: career trajectory, learning agility, ambition, industry trends
persona_pool.personality: Forward-looking and curious. Interested in where candidates want to go, not just where they've been. Tests if they think about the bigger picture.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Where do you see this industry in 5 years, and how does this role fit into your long-term plan?

scenarios.title: Campus Placement — IT Company
scenarios.description: You're a final-year engineering student at a campus placement drive. A mid-size IT company is hiring freshers for their software team.
scenarios.setting: A college seminar hall converted into an interview room. Two interviewers sit behind a desk with your resume printed out.
scenarios.session_topic: Entry-level software developer at a mid-size IT company
coaching_tips: Focus on your projects and internships

storybook_pages.title: The Big Day
storybook_pages.text: It's campus placement season. You've prepared for weeks — mock interviews, resume polishing, reading about the company. Today is the day.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian college student in formal clothes walking toward a campus building with 'Placement Drive' banner, morning sunshine, determined expression, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Waiting Room
storybook_pages.text: Fifteen candidates wait nervously. Some flip through notes, others practice their introductions under their breath. Your number is called.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian students waiting outside interview room in a college corridor, some reading notes, one being called inside, realistic digital art

storybook_pages.title: Your Turn
storybook_pages.text: You take a deep breath, knock on the door, and walk in. Two interviewers smile and gesture to the chair. 'Please, have a seat. Tell us about yourself.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian student entering interview room facing two interviewers behind desk, professional setting in college, warm lighting, digital art

scenarios.title: Startup Interview — Wear Many Hats
scenarios.description: A fast-growing edtech startup is looking for someone who can do a bit of everything. They want hustle, creativity, and a 'get things done' attitude.
scenarios.setting: A colorful coworking space in Bangalore. Beanbags, whiteboards covered in ideas, and the faint sound of coding in the background.
scenarios.session_topic: Generalist role at a fast-growing edtech startup
coaching_tips: Show adaptability and willingness to learn
Give examples of wearing multiple hats

storybook_pages.title: The Startup Hub
storybook_pages.text: You arrive at a coworking space buzzing with energy. Whiteboards full of product roadmaps, engineers in hoodies, and the founder personally greets you.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Modern coworking space in Bangalore with whiteboards and beanbags, Indian startup founder greeting a candidate, vibrant digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Culture Test
storybook_pages.text: Before the formal interview, they ask you to join a team standup. You observe how they communicate — fast, direct, with lots of laughter. This is the culture.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Young Indian startup team in a standup meeting, casual dress, whiteboard with sticky notes, candidate observing, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Interview Begins
storybook_pages.text: The founder sits across from you with just a notebook. 'No structured questions. Just tell me what makes you tick and why you'd thrive here.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian startup founder with notebook interviewing candidate across a small table, coworking space background, casual but focused, digital art

scenarios.title: MNC Corporate — Manager Round
scenarios.description: You're interviewing for a mid-level position at a top multinational company. The hiring manager is experienced and has specific expectations.
scenarios.setting: A glass-walled meeting room on the 15th floor of a corporate tower in Mumbai. The city skyline stretches behind the interviewers.
scenarios.session_topic: Mid-level role at a multinational corporation

storybook_pages.title: The Corporate Tower
storybook_pages.text: The elevator opens on the 15th floor. Glass walls, muted conversations, and the Mumbai skyline. A receptionist hands you a visitor badge.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Modern corporate office lobby on high floor, Mumbai skyline through glass walls, Indian professional receiving visitor badge, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Assessment
storybook_pages.text: You've cleared two rounds already. This is the manager round — the one that really matters. Everything you've prepared comes down to this conversation.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Interview preparation scene, Indian professional reviewing notes in corporate waiting area, glass meeting rooms in background, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Face to Face
storybook_pages.text: The manager walks in — confident, friendly but direct. 'I've read your resume. Now I want to understand how you think. Let's begin.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian senior manager extending handshake to candidate in glass meeting room, Mumbai skyline background, professional digital art

scenarios.title: High-Pressure Interview — Stress Test
scenarios.description: A competitive consulting firm uses stress interviews to test candidates. The interviewer will challenge you, interrupt, and push you to your limits.
scenarios.setting: A minimalist conference room. One interviewer sits with folded arms, barely smiling. The chair feels uncomfortable on purpose.
scenarios.session_topic: Analyst position at a top consulting firm
coaching_tips: Stay calm — they're testing composure, not trying to reject you

storybook_pages.title: The Reputation
storybook_pages.text: Everyone warned you about this firm's interview process. 'They'll try to break you,' said a senior. 'Stay calm and don't take it personally.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Intimidating corporate building exterior, Indian candidate looking up at it with determination, stormy sky, dramatic digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Setup
storybook_pages.text: The waiting room is silent. No small talk. Candidates avoid eye contact. When your name is called, you notice the interviewer doesn't smile.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Tense interview waiting room, Indian candidates sitting apart in silence, minimalist corporate decor, moody lighting, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Game On
storybook_pages.text: You sit down. Before you can even settle in, the interviewer fires: 'You have 30 seconds. Why should I not reject you right now?'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Intense interview moment, stern Indian interviewer leaning forward, candidate sitting upright maintaining composure, minimalist room, dramatic digital art

scenarios.title: Government Panel Interview — UPSC Style
scenarios.description: Face a panel of 3 interviewers in a formal government-style interview. They'll test your general knowledge, current affairs, and ability to think on your feet.
scenarios.setting: A formal government office with wood-paneled walls and a long desk. Three distinguished interviewers sit in a row, each with a different background.
coaching_tips: Be honest if you don't know something
Show balanced perspective on controversial topics
learning_objectives: Demonstrate breadth of knowledge and balanced thinking

storybook_pages.title: Years of Preparation
storybook_pages.text: Three years of preparation have led to this moment. You've cleared Prelims, Mains, and now face the final hurdle — the personality test.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian UPSC aspirant walking toward a grand government building, formal attire, early morning, determination in eyes, realistic digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Panel
storybook_pages.text: Three distinguished panelists — a retired bureaucrat, an academic, and a social scientist. They've interviewed hundreds. They can spot rehearsed answers instantly.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Three distinguished Indian panelists behind a long wooden desk in a formal government office, wood-paneled walls, serious but fair expressions, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The First Question
storybook_pages.text: The chairman opens your dossier, glances at your hobbies, and asks something completely unexpected. Your journey begins.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Close-up of interview panel chairman opening a file, candidate seated across, formal government interview room setting, digital art

transfer_exercises.game_context: Managing resources across multiple rounds to reach the best outcome
transfer_exercises.real_world: Planning study time over a semester rather than cramming before exams
transfer_exercises.challenge: Create a resource management plan for your next month: budget time/money/energy across competing priorities.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from negative events across game rounds
transfer_exercises.real_world: Maintaining performance after setbacks in a sports season or project
transfer_exercises.challenge: Track your energy/mood for 5 days. Notice patterns. What depletes you? What restores you?

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

title: Job Interview
description: Practise real-world job interviews across a range of roles and industries. Learn to present your strengths confidently, handle tricky behavioural questions, and make a lasting impression.
coaching_moment: Practise real-world job interviews across a range of roles and industries. Learn to present your strengths confidently, handle tricky behavioural questions, and make a lasting impression.
cultural_context: India's competitive job market — with millions of graduates competing for limited positions at India's top companies — makes interview preparation a high-stakes skill. This game builds the self-presentation, active listening, and strategic communication needed to succeed.
learning_objectives: Develop critical thinking through negotiation gameplay
Build self-awareness about your strengths and areas for growth
reflection_prompt: Where did you give ground, and where did you hold it? What did the other side teach you about your own priorities?
